title: Unified observability in Amazon OpenSearch Service: metrics, traces, and AI agent debugging in a single interface
key_points: OpenSearch UI now shows Prometheus metrics (PromQL), logs, traces and AI-agent reasoning traces in one observability workspace.
Two demo scenarios: a slow multi-agent app and a failing microservice traced down to the faulty span.
services: Amazon OpenSearch Service, Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus
authors: Muthu Pitchaimani, Raaga N.G, Kevin Lewin, Rekha Thottan

title: Migrate to Apache Flink 2.2 on Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink
key_points: Flink 2.2 on the managed service brings Java 17, a newer RocksDB state backend and SQL-native model inference, but removes the DataSet API, Java 11 and legacy connector interfaces.
Upgrade runs in place with state kept: update code, check state compatibility, enable auto-rollback and snapshots, upgrade, watch, roll back if needed.
Java 11 runtime support ends, so Flink 1.x users will be pushed to move.
services: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink, AWS CloudFormation
decision: Stay on Flink 1.x vs in-place upgrade to 2.2 with auto-rollback for stateful streaming apps
authors: Francisco Morillo, Mayank Juneja

title: Using Apache Sedona with AWS Glue to process billions of daily points from a geospatial dataset
key_points: Adds the Apache Sedona libraries to a Glue Spark job to parse, index and aggregate very large daily flight-position data with spatial SQL, then maps the output in Kepler.gl.
The job is CPU-bound with Python UDFs and single-partition write stages, so adding workers gives diminishing returns.
AWS reports 10 G.1X DPUs finished in about 12 minutes for about USD 0.88, against about 10 minutes and USD 2.34 on 32 DPUs.
services: AWS Glue, Apache Sedona, Amazon S3
decision: More vs fewer vs larger Glue workers for a CPU-bound Spark job that does not scale linearly
authors: Ruan Roloff, Denys Gonzaga, Lucas Vitoreti

title: Analyzing your data catalog: Query SageMaker Catalog metadata with SQL
key_points: Once turned on, SageMaker Catalog writes a daily snapshot of all asset metadata (technical, business, ownership) into an Iceberg table in an S3 table bucket.
Snapshots are partitioned by date, so Athena or notebooks can track registration trends, missing descriptions and classification gaps over time without building an export pipeline.
Base feature behind later catalog-compliance scoring patterns.
services: Amazon SageMaker Catalog, Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, Amazon S3 Tables, Apache Iceberg, Amazon Athena
decision: Managed daily metadata export vs custom API-to-ETL pipelines for catalog health reporting
authors: Ramesh H Singh, Rohith Kayathi, Pradeep Misra, Steve Phillips

title: Configure a custom domain name for your Amazon MSK cluster enabled with IAM authentication
key_points: Puts an NLB with an ACM private certificate and a Route 53 private zone in front of MSK so IAM-authenticated clients can use a company DNS name.
Part 2 of the series; mostly networking setup and an FAQ on broker changes and errors.
services: Amazon MSK, Elastic Load Balancing, AWS Certificate Manager, Amazon Route 53
authors: Mazrim Mehrtens, Mark Taylor, Subham Rakshit

title: Securely connecting on-premises data systems to Amazon Redshift with IAM Roles Anywhere
key_points: On-premises ETL and query tools use X.509 certificates from an existing CA to get short-lived IAM credentials, then swap them for temporary Redshift database credentials; no static keys.
Traffic stays private through VPC endpoints and private DNS, and every credential request lands in CloudTrail.
Compares the usual alternatives (static keys, shared DB users, VPN alone, custom credential brokers) and their weak points; works for provisioned and Serverless.
services: Amazon Redshift, AWS IAM Roles Anywhere, AWS IAM, AWS Private CA, AWS CloudTrail, AWS CloudFormation
decision: Static IAM keys vs shared DB credentials vs IAM Roles Anywhere certificates for on-premises access to Redshift
authors: Zainab Syeda, Kanwar Bajwa, Xiaoxue Xu

title: Migrate third-party and self-managed Apache Kafka clusters to Amazon MSK Express and Standard brokers with Amazon MSK Replicator
key_points: MSK Replicator can now pull from Kafka clusters outside MSK (self-managed, other clouds, Confluent and other Kafka-compatible services) secured with SASL/SCRAM or mTLS, replacing a self-run MirrorMaker 2.
It copies topics, configs and consumer offsets, and runs both ways so applications can be moved over in stages with little downtime.
Steps cover networking, source-side auth, replication health metrics and the order in which to cut over consumers and producers.
services: Amazon MSK, MSK Replicator, MSK Express brokers, Apache Kafka
decision: Self-run MirrorMaker 2 vs managed MSK Replicator for migrating external Kafka clusters to MSK
authors: Ankita Mishra, Mazrim Mehrtens

title: Building unified data pipelines with Apache Iceberg and Apache Flink
key_points: Instead of running a batch pipeline and a separate streaming copy, a Flink job reads only the new snapshots of an Iceberg table so one copy of the data serves both.
Covers when this fits (freshness of seconds to minutes, frequently queried recent data) and when it does not.
Production section on tuning, monitoring, cost, security and troubleshooting the Flink-on-Iceberg reader.
services: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink, Apache Iceberg, AWS Glue Data Catalog, Amazon S3
decision: Separate batch and streaming pipelines vs one Iceberg table consumed incrementally by Flink for minute-level freshness
authors: Nikhil Jha, Kaushal (KK) Agrawal, Vafa Ahmadiyeh, Vyasamaharshi Garigipati

title: Enhancing Identity Intelligence with Babel Street Match and Amazon OpenSearch
key_points: A partner plugin adds multilingual name and entity matching to OpenSearch for screening and investigations, handling spelling variants and transliteration.
Partner marketing with use cases and install steps.
services: Amazon OpenSearch Service, Babel Street Match
authors: Babel Street — Kunal Sharma, Gil Irizarry, Mae Wells-Kress, Craig Harmon

title: Getting started with Apache Iceberg write support in Amazon Redshift – Part 2
key_points: Redshift can now run DELETE, UPDATE and MERGE on Iceberg tables in S3 and S3 table buckets, so row-level changes and upserts no longer need a separate Spark job.
Example is a staging-to-production sync: drop opted-out customers, update customer details, then MERGE staged orders into the target table.
Row-level changes leave merge-on-read delete files behind, so plan compaction with Glue table optimizers or S3 Tables maintenance.
services: Amazon Redshift, Apache Iceberg, Amazon S3 Tables, AWS Glue Data Catalog
decision: Native Redshift tables vs Iceberg tables updated from Redshift vs Spark/Glue MERGE for upserts shared with other engines
attaches_to: dbt-pipelines (incremental merge into Iceberg from Redshift)
authors: Sanket Hase, Ebrahim Salim Hirani, Sherry Xiao, Sundeep Kumar, Ritesh Sinha, Raghu Kuppala, Xiening Dai

title: Get to insights faster using Notebooks in Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio
key_points: Tour of the Unified Studio notebook: Python and SQL in one notebook, many connected sources, scaling out to Athena Spark, and an AI data agent for code and profiling.
Demo runs from a housing-price dataset to a trained ML model; feature walkthrough rather than a design topic.
services: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, Amazon Athena, AWS Glue Data Catalog
authors: Praveen Kumar, Siddharth Gupta, Majisha Namath Parambath

title: Implementing Kerberos authentication for Apache Spark jobs on Amazon EMR on EKS to access a Kerberos-enabled Hive Metastore
key_points: Lets Spark jobs on EMR on EKS get Kerberos tickets from Active Directory so they can share an existing Kerberos-secured Hive metastore with EMR on EC2.
Heavy setup (AD, EKS, VPC peering, keytabs with KMS, TLS on Thrift) for a legacy Hadoop-security niche.
services: Amazon EMR on EKS, Amazon EMR, Apache Hive Metastore, Kerberos, AWS KMS
authors: Krishna Kumar Venkateswaran, Avinash Desireddy, Sunil Chakrapani Sundararaman, Suvojit Dasgupta

title: How to use Parquet Column Indexes with Amazon Athena
key_points: Athena can now use Parquet page-level min/max indexes on Iceberg tables (turned on by a Glue table property) to skip pages inside row groups, not just whole row groups.
Indexes only help when values are clustered, so the post sorts the table on a high-cardinality filter column with an Iceberg rewrite first.
AWS reports, on a 3 TB TPC-DS table, sorting alone cut runtime by about 25% and sorting plus column indexes by about 50%, with bytes scanned down about 71%.
services: Amazon Athena, Apache Iceberg, Apache Parquet, AWS Glue Data Catalog, Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio
decision: Unsorted files vs sorted files vs sorted files plus Parquet column indexes for selective lake queries
attaches_to: aws-bytes: File Layout Optimization (active); dbt-pipelines (Athena + Iceberg folder)
authors: Matt Wong

title: Introducing Amazon MSK Express Broker power for Kiro
key_points: A Kiro power bundles MSK MCP servers with operating guidance so the IDE can help create, size and troubleshoot Express broker clusters in natural language.
Product announcement with install steps; no architecture content.
services: Amazon MSK, Kiro
authors: Stephan Schiller

title: Proactive monitoring for Amazon Redshift Serverless using AWS Lambda and Slack alerts
key_points: A scheduled Lambda reads CloudWatch metrics and runs diagnostic SQL through the Data API to check queued and running queries, RPU usage, storage, connections and slow queries on a Serverless workgroup.
Anything over a configurable threshold goes to SNS and on to Slack via Amazon Q Developer in chat apps; the whole stack is one CloudFormation template.
Advises starting with loose thresholds and tightening them after watching real workload behaviour.
services: Amazon Redshift Serverless, AWS Lambda, Amazon EventBridge, Amazon CloudWatch, Amazon SNS, Amazon Q Developer, AWS CloudFormation
decision: Built-in Serverless dashboards vs CloudWatch alarms vs scheduled metric-plus-SQL checks pushed to chat for Redshift alerting
attaches_to: aws-bytes: Redshift ETL failure alert (planned); dbt-pipelines (Redshift Serverless)
authors: Cristian Restrepo Lopez, Satesh Sonti

title: Introducing workload simulation workbench for Amazon MSK Express broker
key_points: A CDK-deployed workbench that spins up an MSK Express cluster plus configurable producers and consumers to test partition counts, message sizes and load before going to production.
Two modes: test many workload scenarios on one deployment, or redeploy with different broker sizes and compare to right-size.
Positioned for sizing and team training; AWS stresses results are indicative, not a benchmark.
services: Amazon MSK, MSK Express brokers, AWS CDK, Amazon CloudWatch
decision: Guess Kafka sizing from docs vs test partitions, message sizes and broker size against a simulated workload
authors: Manu Mishra, Ramesh Chidirala

title: Modernize business intelligence workloads using AWS Quick
key_points: Reference walk-through that puts AWS Quick on top of either Redshift Serverless or Athena: load sample data, expose business views, then connect them as Quick datasets.
Most of the post is about Quick's generative BI layer: natural-language dashboards, Topics and Spaces, chat agents and automated Flows.
Lists industry use cases such as regulatory reporting and chat over KPI dashboards.
services: AWS Quick, Amazon Redshift Serverless, Amazon Athena
decision: Classic dashboards vs generative BI (topics, chat agents) on top of a Redshift or Athena serving layer
attaches_to: dbt-pipelines (possible BI layer over NYC 311 marts)
authors: Satesh Sonti, Ramon Lopez

title: Streamline Apache Kafka topic management with Amazon MSK
key_points: MSK now has native APIs and console pages to create, change and delete Kafka topics (partitions, replication, retention, cleanup policy) without an admin client.
Topic access can be scoped with IAM, and topics can be declared in CloudFormation so they ship through the same CI/CD as the cluster.
The console adds a per-topic view of partitions, configuration and metrics.
services: Amazon MSK, AWS CloudFormation, AWS IAM
decision: Kafka admin clients or third-party IaC vs native MSK topic APIs in CloudFormation for managing topics
authors: Swapna Bandla, Judy Huang, Mazrim Mehrtens

title: How to set up a network-isolated VPC for Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio
key_points: Runs a SageMaker Unified Studio domain in a VPC with no internet path, reaching every service through interface and gateway endpoints across three AZs.
Mostly a checklist of the endpoints and subnet requirements needed for regulated setups.
services: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, Amazon DataZone, Amazon VPC, AWS PrivateLink
authors: Rohit Vashishtha, Baggio Wong, Saurabh Bhutyani

title: Agentic AI for observability and troubleshooting with Amazon OpenSearch Service
key_points: OpenSearch UI gains a context-aware chatbot, an investigation agent that forms and tests root-cause hypotheses across indices, and a memory that both share.
Aimed at SRE incident work on logs and traces, not data pipelines.
services: Amazon OpenSearch Service, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
authors: Muthu Pitchaimani, Hang Zuo, Mikhail Vaynshteyn

title: Navigating multi-account deployments in Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio: a governance-first approach
key_points: Weighs one account for everything against a central governance account plus associated business-unit accounts, judged on security boundaries, admin overhead and team autonomy.
Project profiles can pin a fixed account and Region (strict compliance) or let users pick from an account pool (dev/test/prod with fewer templates).
Gives a rule of thumb for project boundaries: split by budget owner, access policy and compliance regime, not per pipeline.
services: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, Amazon DataZone, Amazon SageMaker Data & AI Governance
decision: Single account vs central governance account with business-unit accounts (and static vs dynamic project profiles) for a governed data platform
authors: Ben Shafabakhsh, Juan Daza, Adriana Lopez

title: Improve the discoverability of your unstructured data in Amazon SageMaker Catalog using generative AI
key_points: PDFs, images and emails are processed automatically and Bedrock extracts business terms and descriptions that are attached as metadata in SageMaker Catalog, so the files become searchable next to tables.
Part 1 of a series; consuming the enriched assets is left for part 2.
services: Amazon SageMaker Catalog, Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, Amazon Bedrock, Amazon S3
authors: Nishchai JM, Narendra Gupta, Kiki Nwangwu, Ramesh H Singh
